issue_context.title: DRA drivers: helper code for checking device allocations
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

A DRA driver has to check in NodePrepareResources whether the devices are a) already prepared for other claims and b) really currently available.

If so, it has to refuse to prepare them again. This is a sanity check that acts as last line of defense against unintended concurrent usage of a device (case a) or race conditions. DRA tries hard to avoid such situations, but at least the ["device became unhealthy"](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/128979) is inherently racy. Allocating the same device for different claims could be the result of a bug or allocation by different schedulers without [coordination](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/128980#issuecomment-2500948711).

DRA driver authors might forget to implement this check. Perhaps we can move it into [k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/kubeletplugin](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/kubeletplugin) with such an API change that the driver authors are forced to do something?


### Why is this needed?

Higher quality of DRA drivers.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129442 can be used as a starting point. Opens:
- Config option to let DRA drivers opt out of the forced serialization.
- Contextual logging with per-gRPC-call sequence ID.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130700 revises the Go API and provides everything except for forcing DRA drivers to implement claim verification. It gets called out explicitly now. I'm undecided whether that is enough.

review_comments:
You need to document this interface very comprehensively. Describe what DRA driver authors must do and what they can expect from the caller.

This is what they are going to read to figure out how to implement a DRA driver. Assume they know nothing about the KEP.

See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129442#discussion_r1927371680 ("should not use types from the gRPC interface") and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129442#discussion_r1928372933 ("Fetching them [ResourceClaims] then is something that happens once in this package").
Still uses gRPC types in the interface.

For the current implementation here in this PR I agree, because the lock is in the CheckDeviceAllocation which is called from NodePrepareResources, making two concurrent NodePrepareResources pass CheckDeviceAllocation in a tight sequence before either of of them prepares the Resource.

But if the locking was moved to beginning of NodePrepareResources, so the CheckDeviceAllocation wouldn't start until potential parallel NodePrepareResources finishes, - that would solve the problem ?

The global lock should cover both `NodePrepareResources` and `NodeUnprepareResources`, to be sure that checking isn't influence by something that goes on in parallel. I think that would solve the problem.

The question is: do we *want* all `NodePrepareResources` and `NodeUnprepareResources` calls to be serialized? This potentially diminishes throughput because long-running operations cannot overlap.

In theory global lock should be fine, simplifying some things, in our Intel DRA drivers we do the same already now. The only thing I'd be worry about is network-attached devices that could potentially be managed by same driver as local devices - while some devices might take minutes to finish preparing, others would be very fast, but I bet you considered this situation, so I'm fine with it. I don't know if this is a realistic case at all, it just feels a bit imposed to force all DRA drivers to process claims sequentially.

We probably should leave an escape hatch: by default, DRA drivers get calls serialized for them. If they opt out of that, `CheckDeviceAllocation` is not called. The documentation for this opt-out flag must make that very clear.
already add some documentation. Is it necessary  to implement a file lock in DRAPluginServerWrapper, it is up to the dra driver to decide whether to enable it?
This number doesn't help a reader of this API documentation. We need write everything down here.
